what: Presets rendered through the real AudioWorklet in Chrome (OfflineAudioContext, 48 kHz, 51,200 frames, note 60 @ velocity 0.9, noteOff at frame 12,000) — the same signal the Node harness in fmProcessorHeadroom.test.ts renders, so the two can be compared sample-peak to sample-peak.
how: chrome-devtools MCP evaluate_script on the ?debug=1 page: import('/src/audio/presets.ts'), OfflineAudioContext.audioWorklet.addModule('/src/audio/worklet/fm-processor.js'), new AudioWorkletNode(ctx, 'fm-part', { processorOptions: { maxVoices: 16, patch, events, seed? } }).

nodeReference.comment: vitest fmProcessorHeadroom, and the offline 16,384-seed sweep reported on the PR

reads: seed7_a === seed7_b on both pages: the same seed is the same audio in a real AudioWorklet, not only under the Node shim.
seed8 differs from seed7: the seed is actually driving the draws.
unseeded_a !== unseeded_b on both pages: with no seed the processor still free-runs from Math.random, which is the game path and is unchanged.
Every atWorstKnownSeed peak matches the offline sweep to seven decimals, so the four trimmed volumes clear 1.0 by 6.1-6.6% in the browser and not merely in Node.
bass-digital's worstPhases value (0.9393108) is the bound the phase-space search produced; the browser agrees with the harness to four decimals.

The two rendering backends produce identical audio figures, as they must: the AudioWorklet runs on the audio thread and does not touch the GPU. The counters differ only because the two pages started a few seconds apart.
